title: Hypnosis Guide Cards, 1 November
intro: Your hypnosis guide as it is in Git, after my second full read of it (every paragraph, beside your published version) and the read for contradictions you asked for.

The read found 216 things. The 205 in our words (Emulate's or mine) are fixed in the guide already, and so are the eight contradictions in our words; the two-hand practice is taught once now, as you asked. What it found in your own words is here: 2 lines said twice, one suggestion for your fingers script, and one contradiction. Approve, Reject or Revise.

In your own words, only punctuation and a few slips changed without a card (two typos, an "ie." that means "for example", and a label in front of your words that wasn't yours), as you said for commas. The Markdown copy of this page lists each one, before and after.
Your answers save as you click. When you're done, click Copy my answers (or Save them as a file) and send them to me.

suggestions.title: “If you are intoxicated and/or …”

edits.before: Put yourself in a place where you can safely do this, which is not: driving a big machine, swimming with the fishies, or otherwise needing to be alert and functionally responsible for yourself or others. If you are intoxicated and/or more confused than usual, or for whatever reason not able to keep yourself safe, then get some immediate support instead of doing exploratory hypnosis. (The part below called "Already Trancey? Stabilize before dipping deeper." can be used to help orient you if you're already open, but don't use it to make yourself deeper if you're not stable.)
edits.after: Put yourself in a place where you can safely do this, which is not: driving a big machine, swimming with the fishies, or otherwise needing to be alert and functionally responsible for yourself or others. suggestions.what: “intoxicated and/or more confused than usual” becomes “intoxicated and more confused than usual”.
suggestions.why: As it is, being intoxicated is by itself a reason to get support instead of doing exploratory hypnosis. Elsewhere the guide does self-hypnosis on loveyhuasca: your own sessions in Why doing it myself worked better for me, Already Trancey? (for when you’re already open, loveyhuasca first in its list), and Stabilize before you interpret (“Self-hypnosis can be powerful when you are in an altered state of consciousness (e.g. when you’re on loveyhuasca …”). With “and”, the stop is for being intoxicated and more confused than usual, and the rest of the sentence (“or for whatever reason not able to keep yourself safe”) still stops anyone a substance has made unsafe.
suggestions.stays: The rest of step 3 word for word, with its pointer to Already Trancey? for when you’re already open.
suggestions.advice_note: I’d approve: step 3 then agrees with your own sessions and Appendix G, and it still stops anyone who isn’t safe.
suggestions.deciding: Approve uses “and”; Reject keeps “and/or”; Revise lets you write your own.

suggestions.title: “As my dad always said …”

edits.before: Let your response guide you as to what to do next regardless of what the script is expecting. Utilize: use what you have (a thought, sound, movement, or objection) to go to the next place, whatever it is. Learn how to notice what is there. If nothing changes, notice that too. As my dad always said, "Always and in everything, expect the very best. But be prepared to take what you get. The best might come afterwards!" For more on language you can use, see Appendix B, or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction in Let the next response guide you. Either way, keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain.

suggestions.title: “… into a clear state of awareness”
suggestions.where: Make the hypnosis more active, P2

edits.before: “Starting with your eyes open, press your thumb to your forefinger. And as you press your fingers together gently and release, you begin to bring yourself into a place of clearer awareness… again you press your fingers together and release, bringing yourself into an even clearer state of awareness. And again as you press your fingers together and release, you bring yourself into a clear state of awareness. And now you stop pressing your fingers together, and in the first second after you stop pressing your fingers together deliberately, you can notice if there is any sensory echo of the pressing in your fingers, in your breathing, in your attention, or nowhere at all. Just notice, sit up straight and work from this level.”
edits.after: “Starting with your eyes open, press your thumb to your forefinger. And as you press your fingers together gently and release, you begin to bring yourself into a place of clearer awareness… again you press your fingers together and release, bringing yourself into an even clearer state of awareness. And again as you press your fingers together and release, you bring yourself into the clearest state of awareness yet. And now you stop pressing your fingers together, and in the first second after you stop pressing your fingers together deliberately, you can notice if there is any sensory echo of the pressing in your fingers, in your breathing, in your attention, or nowhere at all. Just notice, sit up straight and work from this level.”

suggestions.what: “you bring yourself into a clear state of awareness” becomes “you bring yourself into the clearest state of awareness yet”.
suggestions.why: The script steps up, from “a place of clearer awareness” to “an even clearer state of awareness”, and then back down to “a clear state of awareness”, on the press that should take it furthest. In your published version each press takes you further (“Again — clearer, not sleepier.”). The sentence is in your version of the script (30 October), so it’s yours to decide.
suggestions.stays: The rest of the script, word for word.
suggestions.advice_note: I’d approve: it keeps your words and makes the last press the clearest, as your published script does.
suggestions.found_by: My second full read of the guide, beside your published version (1 November)
suggestions.deciding: Approve uses the new wording; Reject keeps yours; Revise lets you write your own.

suggestions.title: “That's enough for today …”

edits.before: Prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come only as close as is welcome. Try to avoid any language that makes you feel you're not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that's ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else's function). Have the adult part of you run the show. The goal is to make it "good as you" rather than "good as new", not to erase history. Tell your little one, "That's enough for today. We're going back to the life we're building." Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you're an adult now, and come back.
